title: Tabbouleh
subtitle: Lebanese bulgur wheat and herb salad with lemon dressing
excerpt: Authentic tabbouleh is a herb salad with a little bulgur, not a bulgur salad with a little herb. The ratio is the opposite of what most Western recipes suggest.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Lebanese tabbouleh preparations.

recipe.batchNotes: Makes a large batch well; dress only what you will eat immediately as the salad wilts quickly once dressed.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bulgur can be soaked and the vegetables chopped a few hours ahead. Dress and combine just before serving.

content.text: The Lebanese original uses a very small amount of fine bulgur wheat as a background texture: the salad is overwhelmingly parsley and mint, with tomato for juiciness and lemon for brightness. If you have been making tabbouleh with equal parts grain and herb, this version will be a revelation. The parsley must be very finely chopped: thick or roughly torn leaves produce a coarse texture that is hard to eat neatly.

items.prepNote: leaves and fine stems, very finely chopped
very finely sliced, white and green parts

content.text: Soak the bulgur. Place the fine bulgur in a bowl and cover with cold water by 1 cm. Leave for 20 to 30 minutes until softened but still with a slight bite. Drain thoroughly, then spread on a clean tea towel and squeeze out as much moisture as possible.

Chop the herbs. This is the most important and time-consuming step. The parsley and mint must be chopped very finely indeed: not a rough chop, but a fine mince. Use a large, sharp knife and rock it back and forth across the herbs. Gather and re-chop several times until the herbs are almost a fine rubble. This produces the right texture and allows the dressing to coat every piece.

Prepare the tomatoes. Quarter the tomatoes and remove the seeds and their surrounding watery gel: this moisture will waterlog the salad if left in. Dice the tomato flesh very finely, about 5 mm. Season lightly with salt and leave in a sieve for 5 minutes to drain off further liquid.

Combine and dress. In a large bowl, mix the drained bulgur, finely chopped parsley, finely chopped mint, diced tomato and spring onion. Pour over the lemon juice and olive oil. Add the allspice and cinnamon if using. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Toss well.

Rest for 20 minutes. Leave the tabbouleh to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving so the bulgur absorbs the dressing and the flavours meld. Taste and add more lemon or salt. Serve at room temperature as a side dish or with flatbread.

items.symptom: Tabbouleh is watery and the dressing pools at the bottom
items.cause: The tomatoes were not deseeded, or the bulgur was not squeezed dry.
items.fix: Always deseed and drain the tomatoes; squeeze the soaked bulgur in a tea towel. If already dressed and wet, drain in a sieve, pressing gently, and add fresh herbs to freshen it up.

items.symptom: Texture is coarse and the herbs feel tough to eat
items.cause: The parsley and mint were not chopped finely enough.
items.fix: Keep chopping: the herbs need to reach an almost fine rubble. A food processor will over-process and bruise the herbs; stick to a sharp knife.

items.cause: Not enough lemon juice, or lemon used was not very fresh and juicy.
items.fix: Tabbouleh is lemon-forward: add more lemon juice and a little more salt. Use freshly squeezed lemon only; bottled juice tastes cooked and flat.
